surprise.title: 52 years ago today, a hunch in an Ethiopian gully found Lucy, named for a Beatles song
surprise.body: On the morning of November 24, 1974, near the Awash River in Hadar, Ethiopia, paleoanthropologist Donald Johanson dropped his plan to update his field notes and went out with graduate student Tom Gray to search for fossils. After two hours on a hot, dusty plain, he decided on a hunch to check the bottom of a small gully, and spotted an arm bone. More bones followed on the slope: vertebrae, part of a pelvis, ribs, and pieces of jaw. In the end about 40% of one skeleton was recovered, a female Australopithecus afarensis who lived 3.2 million years ago. She stood about 3 feet 7 inches tall and weighed around 64 pounds, with a small brain like a chimpanzee but hips and legs that worked almost exactly like ours, proof that walking upright came before big brains. That night the camp played "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds" loudly and on repeat, and the name stuck. In Ethiopia she is also called Dinkinesh, which means "you are marvellous." The original bones rest in a vault at the National Museum of Ethiopia in Addis Ababa. Back home today runs about 57 to 69 degrees and dry, with sunset at 5:36 PM. Nineteen days until you sail on December 13.
